title: Choosing an immediate-fire action (skip / re-enable) leaves a pending same-row confirm armed — two conflicting actions can dispatch
evidence:
RefcheckSkip ->
  fire_refcheck_slot_action(
    menu_closed,
    call_id,
    "skip",
    ...
RefcheckReEnable ->
  fire_refcheck_slot_action(
    menu_closed,
    call_id,
    "re-enable",
    ...
detail: Flow: open start-confirm on a queued row, reopen the menu, choose Skip — the skip fires but refcheck_confirm stays Some(Start); the confirm still renders and Yes fires a competing start POST. Both endpoints are AD-14-guarded (loser 0-rows -> 409 toast), so no corruption, but the row can dispatch two conflicting actions from one click path.
recommended_fix: In the RefcheckSkip/RefcheckReEnable arms, clear refcheck_confirm (and any same-row edit) when firing, e.g. Model(..menu_closed, refcheck_confirm: None).
